summary: Astrid Zotter is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned her PhD from the University of Leipzig. She held positions at the Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities and Documenta Nepalica around 2018, and at the University of Heidelberg around 2023.

Atsuhiko Yoshida was a religious studies and linguistics scholar who studied at Seikei, Tokyo, and Strasbourg universities, the EPHE, and under mentor Georges Dumézil. He researched at CNRS (ca. 1963–1968) and taught as professor at Seikei (1970) and Gakushuin (2006).
Atsushi Ibuki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Waseda University from circa 1978 to 1982. Around 2007, he served as a professor at Toyo University.

Atsushi Kanazawa is an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (ca. 1971–1983). He taught at the Meteorological College (attested 1989–1990) and held lecturer and associate professor posts at Komazawa University from circa 1987 onward.
Atsushi Kiyozawa is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Delhi. In 1989, he held a lecturer post at Kindai University.

Indology and philosophy scholar Atsushi Uno studied at Kyoto and Banaras Hindu universities under T. R. V. Murti and others. He held academic posts at Shuchiin, Kyoto, Tokai, and Hiroshima universities before becoming professor at Kindai University around 1986.

Atsuuji Ashikaga was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at Doshisha and Kyoto universities under Ryosaburo Sakaki, he held multiple faculty positions at Kyoto University from 1930 and served as Tokai University professor emeritus (ca. 1967–1975).
Atsuyoshi Keika is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He held academic appointments at Otani University, attested as a lecturer in 1990 and as a professor in 2014.

Atul Chandra Chatterjee was an Indology and history scholar who studied under Charles Henry Tawney at Presidency University, at the University of Calcutta, and at King's College, Cambridge. He served in the Indian Civil Service from circa 1897 to 1931.

August Boeckh was a German scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics who studied under Friedrich August Wolf and Friedrich Schleiermacher at Halle. He held professorial posts at the University of Heidelberg (1807–1811) and the University of Berlin (1811–1861).

August Conrady was a Sinology, linguistics, and Tibetology scholar who studied at Würzburg and Leipzig. He taught at Peking University (1903–1904) and held posts at the University of Leipzig from 1891, becoming full professor of Sinology in 1920.

August Dillmann was a scholar of linguistics and religious studies who studied at the University of Tübingen under Heinrich Ewald. He held posts at Tübingen (ca. 1848–1854), Kiel (ca. 1854–1864), Giessen (ca. 1864–1869), and the University of Berlin (ca. 1869–1894).

August Fick was a German linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Göttingen under Theodor Benfey. He later became professor of comparative linguistics at Göttingen in 1876 and full professor at the University of Breslau from 1888 to 1891.

August Fischer was a linguistics scholar who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1886 to 1889. He held a post at the University of Leipzig (ca. 1900–1930) and was a board member of the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft (ca. 1908–1920).

August Friedrich Pott was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at Göttingen and Berlin, where he studied under Franz Bopp. He lectured at Berlin (1830) before serving as professor of general linguistics at Halle from 1833.

August Hermann Francke was a scholar of Tibetology, linguistics, and history who studied at Niesky, Moravian Theological College, and the University of Berlin. He served as a Privatdozent at the University of Berlin beginning in 1922.

August Hjalmar Edgren was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Uppsala, Cornell, Nebraska, and Yale under William Dwight Whitney. He held teaching posts at Yale, Lund, the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, and served as Rector at the University of Gothenburg (1891–1893).

August Johan Bernet Kempers was an archaeology and Indology scholar who studied at Leiden University. He directed the Pusat Penelitian Arkeologi Nasional (ca. 1947–1956) and held posts at the Netherlands Open Air Museum (1958–1971) and University of Amsterdam (1969–1984).

August Leskien was a German linguist who studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Jena under Georg Curtius and August Schleicher. He lectured at Göttingen and Jena before serving as a professor at the University of Leipzig from 1870 to 1915.

August Schleicher was a linguistics and Indology scholar who studied at Leipzig, Tübingen, Erlangen, and Bonn under Heinrich Ewald and Christian Lassen. He held posts at the University of Bonn (1846), University of Prague (1850, 1853), and University of Jena (1857).
